# Jarch

<!-- Generated by weave from binder.toml (conventions 0.1). Do not edit: edit binder.toml and run 'wv binder build'. -->

A customized, riced Arch Linux, built as a re-runnable installer over a vanilla Arch install, plus the `[jarch]` pacman repo that serves its own tools and custom builds. An archiso image comes later and wraps the same installer.

`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file. Current state lives in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md);
decisions live in [docs/adr](docs/adr).

## Commands

```sh
# lint
shellcheck -x install/jarch-install install/lib/*.sh install/stages/*.sh tests/*.sh
tests/offline-install.sh                          # test: stubbed installer in Docker, dry run + install + re-run
tests/check-packages.sh                           # test: every listed package exists
tests/container-install.sh                        # test: real install in an archlinux container
~/.jarch/install/jarch-install --profile desktop  # install
wv binder check                                   # binder
```

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `jarch.conf` | settings: AUR helper, pacman tweaks, [jarch] repo, default profiles, login shell |
| `install/` | `jarch-install` entry point, `lib/common.sh`, `stages/NN-name.sh` run in order |
| `profiles/<name>/` | pacman, aur, jarch, dotfiles, services, user-services, groups, kconfig lists |
| `dotfiles/<pkg>/` | stow packages: bash, starship, hypr, waybar, kitty, rofi, dunst, kde |
| `pkgbuilds/<name>/` | packages served from [jarch]: Jarch's tools and custom builds of upstream packages |
| `tools/` | jarch-manager, jarch-pkg, the jarch-install launcher |
| `tests/` | offline, container and package-existence tests |

## Conventions

- **Commits:** [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`feat(scope): …`, `fix: …`, `docs: …`). Breaking changes say so with `!` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- **Branches:** one branch per task, prefixed by who drives it: `claude/<topic>`, `codex/<topic>`, `feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`. Never commit to `main` directly.
- **Worktrees:** one git worktree per agent (`git worktree add ../<repo>-<agent> -b claude/<topic>`). No two agents write to the same files; a task names the paths it owns.
- **Gates:** run the test and lint commands above before handing off. The pre-commit hooks (`pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg`) run the same checks CI runs; never skip them with `--no-verify`.
- Every installer stage is idempotent: a re-run only does what's missing, and `--dry-run` changes nothing. `tests/offline-install.sh` checks both; keep it passing.
- Shell is checked by `shellcheck -x` (config in `.shellcheckrc`); a new script joins the CI shellcheck list.
- Profiles are data: one item per line in `profiles/<name>/<list>`. A package in a list must exist in the Arch repos or have a PKGBUILD (`tests/check-packages.sh`).
- Never touch the developer's own system in tests: they run in containers or with pacman, makepkg and systemctl stubbed.
- Publishing `[jarch]` and signing keys are owner-only: CI publishes on merge to `main`; never add a real key or publish by hand.

## Working with agents

The full protocol is in [yard/docs/protocol.md](https://github.com/J-wgit/yard/blob/main/docs/protocol.md). In short:

- **Autonomy:** proceed on reversible work (branches, drafts, local files, tests). Stop and ask before irreversible work: deletions, schema changes, publishing (releases, deploys, messages outside the project), secrets, force-pushes.
- **`callout_need`:** you're blocked and need a fact or access. Say exactly what, what it blocks, and what you already tried.
- **`callout_propose`:** you're bringing a decision. Give the options, your recommendation and why, and the cost of being wrong (reversible or not, blast radius).
- **Big work:** spec first, then milestones (M0, M1, M2, …), each with an acceptance check.
- **Review:** the reviewing agent is never the authoring agent. Reviews and handoffs are typed messages (`conventions.api`), not free text.
- **Routing:** Tier 0 tools for deterministic work, Tier 1 small models for single-shot work, Tier 2 reasoning agents for judgement. A failed attempt moves up one tier before it goes to the human.
- **Events:** runs write the shared run-event log (`run-event/v0`) that Callout, Warden, Gatekeeper, Proving Ground and Cohort all read.

## Done means

- The change does what the task asked, and nothing it didn't.
- Tests and lint pass locally with the commands above, and CI is green.
- New behaviour has a test; a bug fix has a test that failed before the fix.
- Docs, `STATUS.md` (via `binder.toml`) and an ADR are updated when the change alters what they say.
- The task ends with a handoff: **what changed, how it was verified, what's uncertain, what's next.**
- shellcheck is clean and `tests/offline-install.sh` passes; a package-list change also passes `tests/check-packages.sh`.
